next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information

glance_notes.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — 2026 Key Election Dates
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration Available: Wyoming's regular voter registration period closes October 19 for the November 3, 2026 General Election, but eligible residents may still register and vote in person during the absentee-voting period and may register and vote at their polling place on Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — 2026 Key Election Dates
glance_notes.text: Absentee Voting Begins October 6: Any qualified Wyoming voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular absentee voting begins October 6. Voters may request an absentee ballot at any time during 2026 before Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Elections FAQs
glance_notes.text: Polls Open 7:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m.: Wyoming polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Wyoming residents may register in person through their County Clerk or other authorized county locations. Registration by mail is also available when the required application, identification, proof of U.S. citizenship and proof of Wyoming residency are submitted; for most domestic applicants, the mailed registration application must be notarized. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on or before the next election, reside in Wyoming and the precinct where registering, and have been a bona fide Wyoming resident for at least 30 days before the election. A person convicted of a felony must have had civil or voting rights restored, and a person adjudicated mentally incompetent is not eligible while that disqualification remains. Wyoming also allows eligible residents to register and vote during the absentee-voting period after the regular registration deadline and at the polls on Election Day.
register.glance_value: In person, by mail and Election Day registration
register.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
register.internal_note: Wyoming's registration rules changed significantly under legislation effective for the 2026 election cycle, including explicit proof-of-citizenship and proof-of-residency requirements. Current Secretary of State guidance requires 30 days of bona fide Wyoming residency. A valid Wyoming driver's license may satisfy multiple requirements if it does not indicate that the holder is not a U.S. citizen. Applicants without a current Wyoming driver's license face additional identification, citizenship and residency documentation requirements.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Wyoming does not provide a statewide public online lookup that displays an individual's voter registration record in the same way some states do. Voters who are unsure whether they are registered should contact their County Clerk. Wyoming's official Voter Information Tool can be used with a residential address to find an Election Day polling place, view statewide ballot information and obtain County Clerk contact information.
check_registration.glance_value: Contact your County Clerk to confirm registration
check_registration.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Elections FAQs
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State's absentee FAQ specifically directs a voter who is unsure of registration status to contact the County Clerk. The Voter Information Tool at [https://myelectionday.sos.wyo.gov/WYVOTES/Pages/VOSearch.aspx](https://myelectionday.sos.wyo.gov/WYVOTES/Pages/VOSearch.aspx) is address-based and provides polling-place, statewide ballot and County Clerk information; do not misrepresent it as a personal registration-status lookup.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Wyoming's regular voter registration period closes Monday, October 19. Eligible residents who miss that deadline may still register in person and cast an absentee ballot from October 20 through November 2. Eligible residents may also register and vote at their polling place on Election Day.
deadlines.glance_value: October 19 regular deadline; registration continues with voting afterward
deadlines.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — 2026 Key Election Dates
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Key Election Dates document explicitly states October 19 as the General Election registration closing date, October 20-November 2 as the period when voters may still register in person and cast an absentee ballot, and November 3 as Election Day registration. Do not describe October 19 as an absolute final registration deadline.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the Wyoming Secretary of State's Voter Information Tool to find your Election Day polling place by residential address. The tool also provides statewide ballot information and County Clerk contact information. Polling-place information is supplied and updated by Wyoming County Clerks, so voters should confirm their location with their County Clerk if they have questions or if a location appears to have changed.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place with the Wyoming Voter Information Tool
polling_place.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Voter Information Tool
polling_place.internal_note: The current state tool says election information is based on residential address and provides polling-place lookup, statewide ballot information and County Clerk contacts. It specifically notes that polling locations are provided and updated by County Clerks and recommends confirming the polling place with the clerk.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Wyoming's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A voter who is in line at 7:00 p.m. is allowed to vote. Wyoming requires voters to show an acceptable form of identification when voting in person. Eligible residents who are not registered may register and vote at their polling place on Election Day after satisfying Wyoming's registration requirements.
election_day.glance_value: 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.; Election Day registration available
election_day.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Elections FAQs
election_day.internal_note: The Secretary of State confirms 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. statewide polling hours and expressly states that the last person in line at 7:00 p.m. may vote. Election Day registration is confirmed by the official 2026 Key Election Dates document. Because 2026 registration now includes citizenship and residency documentation requirements, same-day registrants should be prepared with all required registration documents as well as voter identification.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Wyoming polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line when polls close at 7:00 p.m. is permitted to remain in line and vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Elections FAQs
polling_hours.internal_note: Current Secretary of State election guidance confirms the statewide 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. schedule and the right of voters already in line at closing to cast their ballots.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person / Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: Wyoming does not use a separate statewide early-voting system distinct from absentee voting. Instead, any qualified voter may vote an absentee ballot without providing an excuse, including in person through the County Clerk. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular absentee voting begins October 6. After the regular registration period closes October 19, an eligible unregistered resident may still register in person and cast an absentee ballot from October 20 through November 2. County Clerk office locations and hours vary by county.
early_voting.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
early_voting.internal_note: Wyoming's current law uses a 28-day absentee-voting period rather than the older 40-day period found in outdated Secretary of State PDFs. The official 2026 calendar confirms October 6 as the beginning of General Election absentee voting. Do not use the obsolete 40-day guidance.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any qualified Wyoming voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse. A registered voter may request an absentee ballot from the County Clerk at any time during the 2026 election year before Election Day. Requests may be made through methods provided by the County Clerk, including mail, email, in person or the state's online absentee request system. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular absentee ballots become available October 6. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the County Clerk no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark by Election Day is not sufficient if the ballot arrives after the deadline.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; ballot must arrive by 7:00 p.m. Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current Secretary of State page confirms requests by mail, email, in person and online forms. Any registered voter can receive a regular absentee ballot beginning 28 days before the election. The 2026 Key Election Dates document states absentee requests may be made at any time in 2026 prior to Election Day. The Secretary of State FAQ confirms voted absentee ballots must physically reach the County Clerk by 7:00 p.m. Election Day; late ballots are not counted.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Wyoming voters are required to show an acceptable form of identification when voting in person. Accepted identification includes a Wyoming driver license or state ID card, tribal ID, valid U.S. passport, U.S. military card, driver license or ID card from another state, qualifying University of Wyoming, Wyoming community college or Wyoming public school student ID, valid Medicare or Medicaid insurance card, and a valid Wyoming concealed firearm permit. Medicare and Medicaid cards remain acceptable through December 31, 2029. A voter who does not have an accepted document may obtain a free Wyoming identification card for voting purposes. Voters returning an absentee ballot by mail are not required to provide additional voter identification solely because they are voting by mail.
voter_id.glance_value: Accepted ID required for in-person voting
voter_id.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Voter ID Law
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State Voter ID page explicitly lists accepted IDs and states that Medicare and Medicaid cards remain valid voting IDs until December 31, 2029. It also states that voters mailing absentee ballots do not need additional identification. Registration documentation and Election Day voter ID are separate requirements; new registrants in 2026 must also satisfy Wyoming's citizenship and residency documentation rules.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Wyoming provides voting accommodations for voters with disabilities and elderly voters. Election procedures are intended to allow voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently. A voter whose assigned polling place is inaccessible should contact the County Clerk before the election to request an accommodation or alternative voting arrangement. Available alternatives may include absentee voting before Election Day or another accessible voting arrangement authorized by election officials. Voters who need assistance at a polling place may also request help from election officials as permitted by law.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Contact your County Clerk for accessibility accommodations
accessible_voting.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Voting Information
accessible_voting.flagged_reason: Wyoming's current voter-facing election site provides limited consolidated accessibility guidance. The state's accessibility requirements remain established through election law, HAVA and Secretary of State rules, but voters needing a specific accommodation should confirm current arrangements directly with their County Clerk.
accessible_voting.internal_note: Wyoming Secretary of State accessibility rules provide alternatives for registered voters whose polling places are inaccessible, including absentee voting and other arrangements through the County Clerk. Because some publicly indexed accessibility documents are older administrative materials rather than a dedicated 2026 voter page, avoid making equipment-specific promises without county verification.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Wyoming provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the uniformed services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Military and overseas voters may register and request an absentee ballot using the Federal Post Card Application or Wyoming's applicable forms. Ballots may be requested for delivery by mail, email or fax. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, UOCAVA absentee voting begins September 18. Completed ballots must meet Wyoming's applicable return requirements and be received by the County Clerk no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
military_overseas.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Military/Overseas Citizens Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Calendar identifies September 18 as the start of General Election UOCAVA voting, 45 days before Election Day. Wyoming's current 2026 military/overseas absentee request form allows ballot delivery by email, mail or fax. The FPCA provides temporary registration for one election cycle, while the Wyoming registration form may establish permanent registration. Verify the voter's permitted ballot-return method from current UOCAVA instructions rather than assuming electronic delivery also authorizes electronic return.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Wyoming if they meet the state's voter eligibility requirements, including the requirement to be a bona fide Wyoming resident for at least 30 days before the election and a resident of the precinct where they register. Students must also satisfy Wyoming's current proof-of-citizenship and proof-of-residency requirements when registering. For in-person voting, photo identification issued by the University of Wyoming, a Wyoming community college or a Wyoming public school is among the identification accepted under Wyoming's voter ID law.
student_voting.glance_value: 30-day residency requirement; qualifying Wyoming student IDs accepted
student_voting.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: Do not imply that attending school in Wyoming automatically establishes voting residency. The student must independently satisfy Wyoming's bona fide 30-day residency and precinct-residency requirements. The current Voter ID page specifically accepts University of Wyoming, Wyoming community college and Wyoming public school student IDs for in-person voting.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Wyoming voters can use the Secretary of State's Voter Information Tool to view statewide ballot information associated with their residential address. County Clerks also make sample ballots available before elections. Wyoming law requires sample ballots to be available in the County Clerk's office, posted at polling places and published before primary and general elections. Because local races and ballot questions vary by residence, voters should use their address and County Clerk information to review the ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Use the Voter Information Tool and County Clerk sample ballots
sample_ballot.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Voter Information Tool
sample_ballot.internal_note: The current Voter Information Tool provides statewide ballot information by residential address. Wyoming Election Code §§ 22-6-104 and 22-6-105 require County Clerks to provide and publish sample ballots. Reverify final November 2026 ballot information after General Election ballots are finalized.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Wyoming Secretary of State, Elections Division, Herschler Building East, Suites 100 and 101, 122 West 25th Street, Cheyenne, WY 82002-0020. Phone: 307-777-5860. Email: elections@wyo.gov. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time, Monday through Friday, except official state holidays. For voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot and polling-place questions, voters should contact their County Clerk.
contact.source_name: Wyoming Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Calendar verifies the Elections Division at Herschler Building East, Suites 100 and 101, 122 West 25th Street, Cheyenne, WY 82002-0020; 307-777-5860; [elections@wyo.gov](mailto:elections@wyo.gov). Current Secretary of State pages list office hours as 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Mountain Time Monday-Friday except state holidays. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Wyoming Secretary of State Elections Division, the Wyoming Voter Information Tool and your County Clerk for official election information. These resources provide voter registration requirements, polling-place information, absentee-voting guidance, voter identification requirements, military and overseas voting information, election dates, statewide ballot information and County Clerk contacts. Wyoming County Clerks administer voter registration, absentee ballots, polling places and many other local election functions.
